tier_reason: bench/README.md gives first-party latency/TFLOPS tables against PyTorch SDPA (PyTorch 2.11, CUDA 13.0, L20/H200/B200/H20), produced by the public bench CLI (python -m ffpa_attn.bench; bench/bench_fp8.py, bench/bench_fp4.py). No host CPU or build flags are stated, so C, not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: '1.5x~15x speedup over PyTorch SDPA' for D 320 to 1024. bench/README.md (D=512, PyTorch 2.11, CUDA 13.0): B200 CuTe-DSL forward 6.45x to 8.41x over SDPA (up to 1517 TFLOPS, 16K non-aligned bf16) and backward 8.21x to 14.69x (up to 763 TFLOPS); H200 CuTe-DSL forward 1.81x to 3.46x and backward 4.09x to 6.00x; L20 Triton forward 1.03x (decode) to 1.67x and backward 1.63x to 2.21x; H20 Triton forward 1.57x to 3.46x. README news: FP4 on RTX 5090 850-980 TOPS (D=128-256), '3.8x~4.4x' over PyTorch SDPA (FlashAttention-2 backend); FP8 on L20 '1.5x~1.8x' over PyTorch SDPA (BF16) for D=64~224. Third-party: NVIDIA-NeMo Automodel PR #2436 reports 1.4x~1.5x end-to-end training throughput for Gemma4-31B on 8xH200 (per the README; PR not opened). End-to-end FLUX.1-dev on RTX PRO 5000: 17.19 s (SDPA) vs 16.08 s (FFPA-FP8) and 15.99 s (FFPA-FP4) at 1024x1024; 91.25 s vs 79.91 s and 75.73 s at 2048x2048.
corrections.caveats: For D>256 PyTorch SDPA cannot use its flash backend and falls back to slower backends, so the largest ratios (6x to 15x on B200) are against a weak baseline; FlashAttention-2 does not support D>256 and cuDNN SDPA is not a stated baseline. For D<=256 the speedups are only for FP8/FP4 kernels compared with BF16 SDPA, i.e. lower precision vs higher precision; against SageAttention-2 (FP8) FFPA is only 'comparable or slightly better'. End-to-end diffusion gains are small (about 7% at 1024x1024). First-party; no host CPU or build flags; CUDA backend is forward-only.

corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark with no fla/PyTorch/CUDA versions, build flags or CPU model on the benchmark pages. The H20 page names benchmarks/generate_benchmark_hopper_h20_md.py, which no longer exists (raw fetch 404; the current generator is benchmarks/generate_benchmark_md.py). Both result pages (generated 2026-04-22 and 2026-05-26) predate correctness-related commits: 'fix missing proxy fences around TMA accesses (#25)' (2026-07-29) and 'replace fp16 Neumann inverse with 8x8 fp32 forward substitution' (2026-09-01), so the numbers were measured on code later changed for correctness/precision. H20 is a low-compute, high-bandwidth SKU, so H20 numbers may not transfer to H100. Baseline is the FLA Triton KDA kernel, not oneDNN/cuDNN/XNNPACK/Eigen; the GDN reference is a different (scalar-gate) algorithm, and in one GB200 case (H=64 fixed) FlashKDA is slower than it (0.96x). Only the forward pass is benchmarked; K=V=128 only.
